t: A sultanate founded by Turkic slave soldiers of the Samanids, ruling from Ghazni over Afghanistan, Khurasan and the Punjab.
Mahmud of Ghazni (r. 998–1030) led repeated raids into northern India, sacking the temple of Somnath in 1026.
The Seljuks took Khurasan at Dandanaqan in 1040; the Ghurids burned Ghazni and took Lahore in 1186.
dyk: The scholar al-Biruni, brought to Ghazni after Mahmud conquered Khwarazm, learned Sanskrit and wrote a detailed study of Indian religion, science and customs, completed around 1030.
ev: Sabuktigin is chosen as leader of the Turkic garrison at Ghazni
Mahmud takes Khurasan and is recognised by the Abbasid caliph
Mahmud defeats the Hindu Shahi king Jayapala near Peshawar
Mahmud sacks the temple of Somnath
The Seljuks defeat Mas'ud I at the Battle of Dandanaqan
Ala al-Din Husayn of Ghur sacks and burns Ghazni
The Ghurids take Lahore, ending the dynasty

f.successor: Seljuk Empire (in the west); Ghurid Sultanate
